verdict.root_cause: Three minutes before onset, platform-automation set CART_ADDR=cart:7071 on frontend and, unlike the six identical sets earlier in the week, never reverted it [tr_7698e78df7dd]. Frontend then emits a high-rate gRPC status 14 UNAVAILABLE whose detail is a refused TCP connection to 172.18.0.24:7071 — the exact port in the override — meaning the name resolved and the host was reached but no listener was bound there [tr_98a3591b5fb7]. Cart is healthy throughout, serving per-user requests at info level up to the window edge [tr_f385dc3c5114], with no port or listener change in its history [tr_c7758f64d9bc]. The wrong address value is itself the mechanism; failures propagate to frontend-proxy, load-generator and checkout.
verdict.reasoning: The decisive join is the port: the override names 7071 [tr_7698e78df7dd] and the refused-connection errors name 7071 [tr_98a3591b5fb7]. Connection-refused is an immediate transport rejection, excluding saturation, slowness and DNS failure, and excluding a cart-side freeze or partition since cart logs dense successful work at onset [tr_f385dc3c5114]. Nothing was exhausted and no artifact changed on frontend — its change log holds only env set/revert entries [tr_7698e78df7dd] — while cart had already reverted off its hotfix image 11h earlier with no listener change [tr_c7758f64d9bc]. The six prior sets were each reverted within 8-9 minutes; the seventh was not, which is what distinguishes onset. The interleaved email HTTP 400 on the shipping-quote path is a separate call path with no email change within ~87h [tr_cf6bd139479b]. Both metric baselines failed with HTTP 400 and measured nothing [tr_30019e988363], so the verdict rests on the log/change join alone.
open_questions: Cart's actual listening port was never directly observed — no bind line in its logs [tr_f385dc3c5114] and no service definition read; the inference rests on refusal plus cart's health.
No metrics exist for either service: both baseline queries were rejected [tr_30019e988363], leaving error-ratio onset and restart counts unmeasured.
The email 400 on the shipping-quote path is unexplained and may be a second concurrent fault needing its own fix [tr_cf6bd139479b].

alternatives.root_cause: Cart stopped binding its gRPC listener on 7071, so connections are refused regardless of frontend's configuration.
alternatives.why_not: Cart handles traffic continuously with no restarts or refusals at the window edge [tr_f385dc3c5114], and no port or listener change appears in seven days [tr_c7758f64d9bc]; the only thing that changed near onset was frontend's address value.

alternatives.root_cause: The email service rejects the shipping-quote POST with HTTP 400, breaking checkout-adjacent frontend paths.
alternatives.why_not: It is a different stack frame and call path from the dominant UNAVAILABLE errors [tr_98a3591b5fb7], and email's last change was ~87h before onset and was a revert off the quote image [tr_cf6bd139479b], so it does not explain onset timing.

proposal.expected_effect: After frontend is restored to its prior environment (CART_ADDR unset, as it stood after each of the six earlier reverts) and recreated, the high-rate repeating gRPC 'code: 14 UNAVAILABLE' lines in {service="frontend"} whose detail names a refused TCP connection to :7071 should stop appearing in Loki within a couple of minutes of the container coming back, and frontend cart-path requests should return to succeeding. Confirmation must come from logs, not metrics: both Prometheus baselines were rejected with 400 [tr_30019e988363], so there is no error-ratio series to watch. The secondary signal is the alerted callers — frontend-proxy, load-generator and checkout — ceasing to log cart-path failures; cart should continue its unbroken info-level cart-store stream [tr_f385dc3c5114] and simply receive the traffic again.
proposal.if_wrong: If, five minutes after the recreate, {service="frontend"} still emits connection-refused 14 UNAVAILABLE at the same rate — whether to :7071 or to some other cart address — the diagnosis is wrong: cart's real listening port was never directly observed (no bind line in its logs [tr_f385dc3c5114], no service definition read), so the assumption that the unset default points at a bound listener is inference, not measurement. A second falsifier: platform-automation re-sets CART_ADDR within minutes, in which case this is a loop in the automation and the fix is outside this system. Note also that the email 400 on the shipping-quote path [tr_cf6bd139479b, tr_98a3591b5fb7] is a separate fault and will NOT clear from this action; its persistence is expected and is not evidence against this proposal.
proposal.risk: Recreating frontend drops every in-flight request and connection on the user-facing path for the duration of the recreate — a short, total frontend outage, deliberately taken. If the override was in fact correct and cart had genuinely moved to 7071 while something else refused the connection, this revert points frontend at a stale address and the incident persists with an added outage. Because the override has been set and reverted seven times by automation in a week, a revert without disabling that automation may be undone again within minutes, which would make the result ambiguous rather than conclusive. The email/shipping-quote 400 is untouched and checkout will keep failing on that path.
proposal.blast_radius: frontend only is modified. Its callers see the reset while the container recreates: frontend-proxy, load-generator and checkout (all seed/alerted). Because the reverted value is a dependency address, cart sees cart-path traffic move back to its default endpoint; frontend's other downstreams — ad, product-catalog, product-reviews, recommendation — see their connections reset and re-established but no address change.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Multiple user-facing services alerted simultaneously at critical severity with checkout following a minute later, which is a real customer-impacting failure. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the alert pattern alone does not single out a fault class.
